Cellular IMSI catchers · P25 voice traffic · Visual ID (uniforms/markings)
What an attacker gets from it

Personal-device tracking is its own field
Cellular IMSI catchers, P25, encrypted radio
An attacker with line of sight wins
SCOPE STATEMENT — read this before claiming "officer untrackability"
NULLWEAR mitigates the per-officer Axon BLE identity layer, in the protected zone around a NULLWEAR/P, /V or /S device, against
passive RF observers. It does not, and cannot, defeat: (a) crowd-sourced police-presence reporting via consumer apps; (b) ALPR / visual / human
tracking of marked vehicles or uniformed officers; (c) cellular-side surveillance; (d) tracking of the officer's personal phone or wearables; (e) the
environmental BLE fingerprint of the location they're in. Three of the five mitigated layers can also be closed by an Axon firmware change (RPA + payload
randomisation + dropping jurisdiction-encoding in MAC[3]) — once shipped, NULLWEAR's role is reduced. Don't sell this as universal coverage.
